# Annotation overview 

This report shows a summary of the cell type annotations assigned by `ews-nf`. 

* First, normal cell types were assigned based on their consensus consensus cell type annotations output by `scpca-nf`.
More information on how consensus cell types are assigned can be found in the [ScPCA Portal documentation](https://scpca.readthedocs.io/en/stable/processing_information.html#cell-type-annotation). 
* All immune and endothelial cells are pooled across samples to create a "normal" reference used with `InferCNV` and `AUCell`.
* Tumor cells are those with a total CNV z-score or presence of a Ewing-specific CNV (chr1 gain, chr8 gain, chr16 gain, or chr16 loss) above a specified threshold. 
  * Here, tumor cells were labeled using three different thresholds, > 2, > 1, or > 0
  * All three classifications are shown in the plots below, with the CNV z-score > 2 being the most stringent. 
* Tumor cells are then classified using results from `AUCell`. 
Cells labeled `tumor-high` or `tumor-low` if they have a `EF-activated` z-score > `r params$marker_gene_cutoff` or `EF-repressed` z-score > `r params$marker_gene_cutoff`, respectively. 
Cells labeled `tumor` do not meet either criteria. 


```{r setup, message = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
# knitr options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE
)

library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Set default ggplot theme
theme_set(
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(rep(20, 4)),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent")
    )
)

# settings
options(
  dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE, 
  readr.show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Set seed
set.seed(params$seed)

marker_gene_cutoff <- params$marker_gene_cutoff

# define a umap theme
umap_theme <- function() {
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
      legend.justification = "top"
    )
}

```

<!--Source functions used for plotting:

marker_gene_dotplot()
plot_density()
-->
```{r, child=params$plotting_functions_file}

```


```{r}
# file checks 
stopifnot(
  "sce file does not exist" = file.exists(params$sce_file),
  "annotations results file does not exist" = file.exists(params$annotations_results_file),
  "infercnv heatmap file does not exist" = file.exists(params$infercnv_heatmap_file),
  "validation groups file does not exist" = file.exists(params$validation_groups_file),
  "marker genes file does not exist" = file.exists(params$marker_genes_file),
  "color palette file does not exist" = file.exists(params$color_palette_file)
)
```


```{r, message=FALSE}
# read in sce 
sce <- readr::read_rds(params$sce_file)

# read in annotations results 
annotations_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$annotations_results_file)

# validation groups and marker gene table urls 
validation_groups_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$validation_groups_file) |> 
  # rename final assigned group to avoid conflicts when merging in marker gene expression 
  # we want to separate the marker gene group from the actual cell type annotation
  dplyr::select(consensus_annotation, broad_celltype_group = validation_group_annotation)

# read in validation markers
markers_df <- readr::read_tsv(params$marker_genes_file) |> 
  # only keep genes unique to a single cell type except HPC which doesn't have any unique genes
  # for HPC we keep all 6 marker genes
  dplyr::filter(gene_observed_count == 1 | validation_group_annotation == "hematopoietic precursor cell")

# define color palette
celltype_colors <- readr::read_tsv(params$color_palette_file) |> 
  tibble::deframe()
# add greys for unknown and other 
celltype_colors[["unknown"]] <- "gray60"
celltype_colors[["other"]] <- "black"
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# get coldata for umap 
coldata_df <- scuttle::makePerCellDF(
    sce,
    use.coldata = c("barcodes", "sum", "detected", "subsets_mito_percent"),
    use.dimred = "UMAP"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
      "UMAP1" = "UMAP.1",
      "UMAP2" = "UMAP.2",
      "genes_detected" = "detected"
    ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    unique_id = params$unique_id,
    cell_id = glue::glue("{unique_id}_{barcodes}")
  ) 

annotations_df <- annotations_df |> 
  # add coldata into annotations dataframe
  # this keeps all library cells and all reference cells
  dplyr::full_join(coldata_df, by = c("cell_id", "barcodes", "unique_id")) |> 
  # now validation groups for plotting
  dplyr::left_join(validation_groups_df, by = c("consensus_celltype_annotation" = "consensus_annotation")) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = contains("tier"),
    names_to = "annotation_tier",
    values_to = "ews_annotation"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    ews_annotation = forcats::fct_relevel(ews_annotation, "Unknown", after = Inf),
    broad_celltype_group = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(ews_annotation, "tumor") ~ ews_annotation,
      is.na(broad_celltype_group) ~ "unknown",
      .default = broad_celltype_group
    ) |> 
      forcats::fct_relevel("unknown", after = Inf),
    # use this when making plots that look at tumor high, tumor low vs normal 
    detail_tumor_category = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(broad_celltype_group, "tumor"),
      broad_celltype_group,
      "non-malignant"
    ),
    # use for just tumor vs normal 
    tumor_category = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(broad_celltype_group, "tumor"),
      "tumor",
      "non-malignant"
    ),
    # include a column with the annotation of all reference cells in one group 
    # use for density plots confirming high AUC/CNV in tumor cells vs. reference
    reference_category = dplyr::if_else(
      ref_or_query == "reference",
      "reference",
      ews_annotation
    )
  )
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# get the total counts for each group and add a column to use for labeling plots 
celltype_counts_df <- annotations_df |>
  dplyr::select(cell_id, annotation_tier, reference_category) |> 
  dplyr::add_count(annotation_tier, reference_category) |> 
  # add in y label 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = glue::glue("{reference_category} ({n})"),
    # classify based on malignant or not malignant
    tumor_category = dplyr::if_else(stringr::str_detect(reference_category, "tumor"), "tumor", "non-malignant") |> 
      factor(levels = c("tumor", "non-malignant"))
  ) |> 
  dplyr::select(-cell_id) |> 
  dplyr::distinct()

# grab order of cell types based on cell type categories that will be plotted in the density plots
celltype_levels <- celltype_counts_df |> 
  dplyr::arrange(tumor_category) |> 
  dplyr::pull(y_label) |>
  unique() |> 
  as.character() 

# pull out reference label to set at the end of the factors 
# this ensures the reference group is always at the bottom of the plot
ref_label <- celltype_levels[stringr::str_detect(celltype_levels, "reference")]
non_ref_labels <- celltype_levels[celltype_levels != ref_label]

# combine everything into one df including counts
all_info_df <- annotations_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_counts_df) |> 
  dplyr::filter(n >= 3) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_label = factor(y_label, levels = rev(c(non_ref_labels, ref_label)))
  )
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# names of split lists to use for mapping
cnv_names <- c("CNV z-score > 0", "CNV z-score > 1", "CNV z-score > 2")

# first split all cells for plots that include reference cells
all_df_list <- split(all_info_df, all_info_df$annotation_tier) |> 
  purrr::set_names(cnv_names) |> 
  rev() |> 
  purrr::map(\(df){
    # for each annotation tier, get a lumped category with the top 8 celltypes
    df <- df |> 
      dplyr::mutate(
        broad_celltype_group_lumped = forcats::fct_lump_n(broad_celltype_group, 8, other_level = "other", ties.method = "first") |>
          forcats::fct_infreq() |>
          forcats::fct_relevel("unknown", "other", after = Inf),
      )
  })

# create a copy of the information for just the library cells
library_df_list <- all_df_list |> 
  purrr::map(\(df) dplyr::filter(df, unique_id == params$unique_id))
```


# Cell type annotation summary

This section summarizes the annotations across all three CNV cutoffs used. 
For simplicity, non-malignant cell types are grouped into broader cell type groups, e.g., all T cell types will be grouped together as T cells for the plots shown in this report. 

## Tables {.tabset}

```{r}
# vector of annotation columns to use for printing out tables and umaps 
tier_cols <- c(
  "CNV z-score > 0" = "tier0",
  "CNV z-score > 1" = "tier1",
  "CNV z-score > 2" = "tier2"
)
```

```{r, results='asis'}
library_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
    
    print(glue::glue('### {title}'))
    
    df |> 
      dplyr::count(ews_annotation, broad_celltype_group, name = "Total") |> 
      # first arrange by total counts
      dplyr::arrange(desc(Total)) |> 
      dplyr::mutate(
        # set order so that all annotations are first ordered by counts and then unknown is last
        ews_annotation = factor(ews_annotation, levels = ews_annotation ) |> 
          forcats::fct_relevel("Unknown", after = Inf)
      ) |>
      # arrange by levels
      dplyr::arrange(ews_annotation) |> 
      knitr::kable() |> 
      print()
  })
```


## UMAPs {.tabset}

The below UMAPs shows the top 8 broad cell type groups. 
The first UMAP shows all cells together and the second UMAP is faceted by cell type, where the cells belonging to the specified cell type are in color and all other are in light grey. 
Any cells labeled with "other" include all normal cells that are not part of the top 8 cell type groups. 


```{r, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
library_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
     
    # one umap with all cells colored by annotation
    single_umap <- ggplot(df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = broad_celltype_group_lumped)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.2) +
      scale_color_manual(values = celltype_colors) +
      umap_theme() +
      guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
      labs(color = "Broad cell type group") 
    
    # facet by annotation
    faceted_umap <- faceted_umap(
      df,
      annotation_column = broad_celltype_group_lumped,
      celltype_colors = celltype_colors,
      point_size = 0.2
    )
    
    # print out plots in each tab
    print(glue::glue('### {title}'))
    print(single_umap)
    print(faceted_umap)
    cat("\n\n")
    
  })
```

## Expression of marker genes in consensus cell types

This section looks at expression of a set of marker genes for each consensus cell type across all cells. 
Here we show any cells that were given a consensus cell type label. 

The dot plot shows the mean expression and percent of cells expressing the marker gene for cells from each broad cell type group. 
The y-axis includes marker genes for each cell type. 
Marker genes are obtained from the list of Human cell markers on [`CellMarker2.0`](http://www.bio-bigdata.center/CellMarker_download.html). 
All marker genes shown were specific to a single cell type, with the exception of hematopoietic precursor cells, if present, which express genes found in other, more differentiated immune cells. 

We expect that each cell type group should show high expression of marker genes associated with that cell type compared to all other cells in the dataset. 

Note that dots are only shown if the gene has mean expression > 0 and is expressed in at least 10% of the cells in the given cell type. 

```{r}
# extract gene expression for marker genes from SCE 
# list of all marker genes
all_markers <- markers_df |>
  dplyr::pull(ensembl_gene_id) |>
  unique()

# we only care about if that gene is expressed otherwise we won't waste memory and include it
expressed_genes <- rowData(sce) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(detected > 0) |>
  dplyr::pull(gene_ids)

# get markers that are expressed
expressed_markers <- intersect(all_markers, expressed_genes)

# get logcounts from sce for expressed genes
gene_exp_df <- scuttle::makePerCellDF(
  sce,
  features = expressed_markers,
  assay.type = "logcounts",
  use.coldata = "barcodes",
  use.dimred = FALSE
) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with("ENSG"), names_to = "ensembl_gene_id", values_to = "logcounts") |>
  dplyr::mutate(detected = logcounts > 0,
                unique_id = params$unique_id) 

# Join all consensus results and marker gene info
all_info_df <- annotations_df |>
  dplyr::filter(unique_id == params$unique_id) |> 
  # only want to look at cells annotated with a normal cell type
  dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(broad_celltype_group, "tumor") | broad_celltype_group == "unknown") |> 
  dplyr::select(barcodes, unique_id, broad_celltype_group) |> 
  dplyr::distinct() |> 
  dplyr::left_join(gene_exp_df, by = c("barcodes", "unique_id")) |>
  # add marker gene information (associated validation group annotation, gene observed count, percent tissues)
  # account for the same gene being present in multiple cell types
  dplyr::left_join(markers_df, by = "ensembl_gene_id", relationship = "many-to-many")
```


```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=15, results='asis'}
# only make the plot if there are any normal cells that were annotated 
if(dim(all_info_df)[2] > 0){
  marker_gene_dotplot(
    consensus_df = all_info_df,
    validation_groups_df = validation_groups_df,
    markers_df = markers_df,
    celltype_colors = celltype_colors,
    min_cells = 0 #TODO: Update this if needed to remove some cell types
  ) 
}
```


# Validation of tumor cells

The below section explores the tumor cell annotations. 
We expect that tumor cells have both high CNV scores and high expression of `EWS::FLI1` target genes, indicated by high z-scores for `EF-activated` and `EF-repressed` gene sets. 

## UMAPs {.tabset}

Here we show UMAPs colored by the mean z-score for either the gene set category or sum CNV.
The UMAP is faceted by cell type category so that only cells from that category are included in the panel. 


```{r, results='asis', fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
all_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
    
    # pivot to have all gene sets and total CNV in a single column for faceting
    umap_df <- df |> 
      tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("EF-activated", "EF-repressed", "EMT-ECM", "cnv_zscore"),
                          names_to = "method_category", 
                          values_to = "zscore") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # remove zscore from cnv_zscore
        method_category = stringr::str_remove(method_category, "_zscore")
      )
    
    # faceted umap looking at non-malignant across tumor categories
    umap <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = zscore)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.2) +
      facet_grid(rows = vars(method_category),
                 cols = vars(detail_tumor_category)) +
      scale_color_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
      labs(color = "Mean z-score") +
      umap_theme() 
    
    print(glue::glue('### {title}'))
    print(umap)
    cat("\n\n")
      
  })
```


## Scatter plot

The scatter plot below shows the z-score for the repressed (`EF-repressed`) vs. activated (`EF-activated`) gene sets in each cell.
The points are then colored by the total CNV score. 

We expect tumor cells to have high CNV scores and high expression of `EWS::FLI1` targets. 
The dotted lines in the plots indicate a z-score of `r marker_gene_cutoff`, i.e. `r marker_gene_cutoff` standard deviations above the mean. 

Any cells with a z-score > `r marker_gene_cutoff` are labeled as `tumor-high` (`EF-activated`) or `tumor-low` (`EF-repressed`). 

```{r}
scatterplot_df <- annotations_df |>
  # only plot values for cells in this library
  dplyr::filter(unique_id == params$unique_id) |> 
  dplyr::select(barcodes, `EF-activated`, `EF-repressed`, cnv_zscore) |> 
  dplyr::distinct()

ggplot(scatterplot_df, aes(x = `EF-activated`, y = `EF-repressed`, color = cnv_zscore)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    x = "EF-activated z-score",
    y = "EF-repressed z-score",
    color = "Total CNV"
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = marker_gene_cutoff, lty = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = marker_gene_cutoff, lty = 2)
```

# Individual methods results 

## `AUCell` summary {.tabset}

The plots in this section will look at the results from running [`AUCell`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/AUCell.html) across a set of gene sets obtained from `MSigDB` and custom gene lists. 
Information about the gene sets used here can be found in [`ews-nf/genesets`](https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/ews-nf/tree/main/genesets). 

Plots here show the z-score calculated from the AUC reported by `AUCell`. 

For each gene set, the mean and standard deviation of the AUC values for all reference cells was used to contain a z-score for all cells. 
The reference was created by pooling all cells across all samples of interest that were assigned a consensus cell type listed as a reference cell type (see [`references/reference-celltype.tsv`](https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/ews-nf/blob/main/references/reference-celltypes.tsv)). 
We then calculated the mean z-score for all gene sets in a given gene set category (e.g., all gene sets that are part of `EF-activated`). 

Gene sets can be divided into three groups to help distinguish tumor cells from normal cells:  

* `EF-activated`: These gene sets contain genes that are activated by the fusion gene, `EWS::FLI1`. 
* `EF-repressed`: These gene sets contain genes that are repressed by the fusion gene, `EWS::FLI1`. 
* `EMT-ECM`: These gene sets contain genes that are found to be highly expressed in tumor cells with low expression of `EWS::FLI1`.

For the plots below all reference cells across all samples are shown alongside all query cells from `r params$unique_id`. 

Cell types are colored based on whether or not the cell type is classified as tumor or non-malignant. 
Any cell type with less than 3 cells will not be included in the plot. 

```{r}
# only have tumor and non-malignant
tumor_category_colors <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n = 2, name = "Dark2")
names(tumor_category_colors) <- c("tumor", "non-malignant")
```


```{r, results='asis', fig.width=8, fig.height=15, message=FALSE}
all_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
    
    # pivot to include all gene sets in their own category
    ridges_plot_df <- df |> 
      tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("EF-activated", "EF-repressed", "EMT-ECM"),
                          names_to = "geneset_category",
                          values_to = "mean_category_zscore")
    
    # faceted ridge plot for each gene set category
    ridge_plot <- ggplot(ridges_plot_df, aes(x = mean_category_zscore, y = y_label, fill = tumor_category)) +
      ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
      facet_wrap(vars(geneset_category),
                 ncol = 1,
                 scales = "free_x") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = tumor_category_colors) +
      labs(
        x = "Mean z-score",
        y = "Broad cell type group",
        fill = "Tumor \ncategory"
      ) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = marker_gene_cutoff, linetype = "dashed")
    
    print(glue::glue('### {title}'))
    print(ridge_plot)
    cat("\n\n")
    
    
  })
```


## `inferCNV` summary

[`inferCNV`](https://github.com/broadinstitute/inferCNV/wiki) was run using all normal cell types that are listed in [`references/reference-celltype.tsv`](https://github.com/AlexsLemonade/ews-nf/blob/main/references/reference-celltypes.tsv) as a reference. 

### Heatmap 

Below is the heatmap showing chromosome gains and losses as output by `inferCNV`. 

![](`r params$infercnv_heatmap_file`)


### All CNVs {.tabset}

Below we look at the distribution of total CNVs detected per cell. 
The number of chromosomes with a detectable CNV is totaled and then the mean and standard deviation of the total CNV sum for all reference cells are used to calculate a z-score for all cells in the dataset. 

As with the `AUCell` results, cell types are colored based on whether or not the cell is classified as tumor or non-malignant. 
All reference cells belonging to the pooled reference are shown in the plots below. 


```{r, results='asis', message = FALSE}
all_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
    
    # extract the cutoff to add a line to the plot
    cutoff <- stringr::word(title, -1, sep = " ") |> as.numeric()
    
    # total CNV across cell types
    total_cnv_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = cnv_zscore, y = y_label, fill = forcats::fct_rev(tumor_category))) +
      ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = tumor_category_colors) +
      labs(
        x = "Total CNV z-score",
        y = "",
        fill = "Cell type \ncategory"
      ) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed")
    
    print(glue::glue('#### {title}'))
    print(total_cnv_plot)
    cat("\n\n")
    
  })
```


### Ewing-specific CNVs {.tabset}

There are a few known copy number variations in Ewing's sarcoma: 

- Gain of Chr8
- Gain of Chr12
- Gain of Chr1p
- Loss of Chr16q

Although these are the most frequent, there are patients who do not have any of these alterations and patients that only have some of these alterations. 
See [Tirode _et al._ 2014](https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-14-0622) and [Crompton _et al._ 2014](https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-13-1037)

Below we look at the presence of these specific CNVs in tumor and non-malignant cells.

```{r, results='asis', message = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=8}
all_df_list |> 
  purrr::iwalk(\(df, title){
    
    # extract the cutoff to add a line to the plot
    cutoff <- stringr::word(title, -1, sep = " ") |> as.numeric()
    
    # put all chromosomes in the same column to plot
    cnv_df <- df |> 
      tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("chr1_gain_zscore", "chr8_gain_zscore", "chr12_gain_zscore", "chr16_loss_zscore"),
                          names_to = "chromosome",
                          values_to = "zscore") |> 
      dplyr::mutate(
        # make the facet labels prettier
        chromosome = stringr::str_remove(chromosome, "_zscore")|> 
          stringr::str_replace("_", " ") |> 
          factor(levels = c("chr1 gain", "chr8 gain", "chr12 gain", "chr16 loss"))
      )
      
    
    # faceted by chromosome
    cnv_plot <- ggplot(cnv_df, aes(x = zscore, y = y_label, fill = tumor_category)) +
      ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5) +
      facet_wrap(
        vars(chromosome),
        scales = "free_x"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = tumor_category_colors) +
      labs(
        x = "Proportion CNV",
        y = ""
      ) +
      theme(legend.position = "none") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed")
    
    print(glue::glue('#### {title}'))
    print(cnv_plot)
    cat("\n\n")
    
  })
```


## QC plots

The below plots will look at some quality control metrics across groups of cells. 
In particular, we want to see if the various tumor cell categories have an underlying technical difference that could be contributing to those cells having either lower CNV scores or lower marker gene expression. 
We will look at the total number of genes detected, total counts, and percentage of mitochondrial reads across the cell types using the results from the CNV z-score > 2 annotations only. 
The red bar indicates the median. 

```{r, fig.width=8}
# get the qc columns and name by the label to use for the y axis
qc_columns <- c(
  "Number of genes detected" = "genes_detected",
  "Total counts" = "sum",
  "Percentage of mitochondrial reads" = "subsets_mito_percent"
)

# for each qc column, make a sina plot and then combine into one plot 
qc_columns |>
  purrr::imap(\(column, y_label){
    
    ggplot(library_df_list$`CNV z-score > 2`, aes(x = detail_tumor_category, y = !!sym(column))) +
      ggforce::geom_sina(size = 0.3) +
      # add median diamond
      stat_summary(
        color = "red",
        geom = "crossbar",
        fun = "median"
      ) +
      labs(
        x = "",
        y = y_label
      ) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
      )
  }) |> 
  patchwork::wrap_plots()
  
```
